title: Simultaneous parameter roots trivialize an invertible-order punctured torsor
statement:
Let $R$ be a strictly henselian regular Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in\mathfrak m$, for $r\geq0$, extend to a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], and put $f=\prod_i t_i$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[1/f]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $G$ be a finite group, $n=|G|$, assume $n$ invertible in $R$, and let $P\to U$ be a finite etale $G$-torsor, not necessarily connected [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Set
$$B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r),\qquad U_B=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$$
[def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. There is an isomorphism over $U_B$
$$P\times_U U_B\simeq\coprod_{g\in G}U_B.$$
Here the isomorphism is of schemes over $U_B$; no equivariance is required [def-pc-fibre-product]. This includes $r=0$, where $B=R$ and $f=1$. No normalization or quotient description of $P$ is included in the conclusion.

proof.text: A finite group has positive order, so $n\geq1$. Choose a generator $\zeta$ of $\mu_n(R)$ using the strict-local roots-of-unity theorem. Its powers other than $1$ have unit difference from $1$, giving exactly the hypotheses of the simultaneous-root structure theorem. That theorem makes the displayed $B$ a strictly henselian regular Noetherian local domain, finite free over $R$, and makes $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ a finite separable extension of $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. We use only these structure assertions, not any quotient classification or torsor splitting.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed pp.133--134, simultaneous-root algebra and essential surjectivity; algebraic expansion of the Abhyankar input.

proof.text: Write $P_B=P\times_U U_B$. Pullback of a finite etale $G$-torsor is again such a torsor, so $P_B\to U_B$ is finite etale and surjective. Apply the field-torsor decomposition to $P_K=P\times_U\operatorname{Spec}K$: its coordinate algebra is $\prod_j L_j$, where each $L_j/K$ is finite Galois of degree dividing $n$. On base change to $E$ this becomes a product $D=\prod_a F_a$ of finite separable extensions of $E$, again by the field-torsor theorem applied to $(P_B)_E$. Each $F_a$ is a field factor of some $L_j\otimes_K E$. The decompositions here are decompositions of the actual generic fibres over their structural maps.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed pp.133--134, simultaneous-root algebra and essential surjectivity; algebraic expansion of the Abhyankar input.

proof.text: The localizations of the regular local ring $B$ are regular local, so $B$ is a regular ring and hence normal. For each $a$, let $C_a$ be its integral closure in $F_a$. The finite-separable integral-closure theorem makes each $C_a$ finite over $B$; put $C=\prod_a C_a$. This constructs a finite normalization in the generic algebra $D$. In particular no excellence assumption is being inserted: the finiteness theorem requires only Noetherian normality and separability, all established here.

Let $T$ be the finite $B[1/f]$-algebra of $P_B$. The generic-algebra injection theorem embeds $T$ into some finite etale $E$-algebra. Thus nonzero elements of $B[1/f]$ act injectively on $T$, so the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_{B[1/f]}E=D$ is injective. This $D$ is its total quotient algebra: all nonzero base elements are nonzerodivisors, and if an element $z\in T$ had a zero field coordinate in $D$, a nonzero idempotent $e$ supported on that coordinate could be written $t/b$ with $t\in T$, $0\ne b\in B[1/f]$, giving $0\ne t$ and $zt=0$. Hence every nonzerodivisor of $T$ is invertible in $D$. By etale ascent of normality $T$ is normal, since $B[1/f]$ is regular and normal. Normal rings are integrally closed in their total quotient rings. The finite-algebra integrality theorem makes $T$ integral over $B[1/f]$. Since $T$ is integral over $B[1/f]$, the integral closure of $B[1/f]$ in $D$ is therefore $T$: an element integral over the base is also integral over $T$, so lies in $T$, and the reverse inclusion is immediate. Integral closure commutes with localization, giving $C[1/f]=T$ and thus $\operatorname{Spec}C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}U_B\cong P_B$ over $U_B$.

source.place: Tag 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize); Tag 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed); etale ascent of normality.

proof.text:
For each $i$, the regular-parameter quotient theorem makes $R/(t_i)$ regular local, with the remaining $t_j$ extending to parameters there. The strict-henselian quotient theorem makes $R/(t_i)$ strictly henselian as well. The image of $\zeta$ retains its root and unit-difference identities. Apply the same simultaneous-root structure theorem to this quotient and the $r-1$ remaining parameters. Its algebra is exactly
$$B/(x_i)\cong (R/(t_i))[x_j:j\ne i]/(x_j^n-\bar t_j:j\ne i).$$
It is a domain, finite free over $R/(t_i)$. Consequently $\mathfrak p_i=(t_i)$ and $\mathfrak q_i=(x_i)$ are prime, $\mathfrak q_i\cap R=\mathfrak p_i$, and both parameters are nonzerodivisors. These assertions also cover $r=1$, where the quotient root construction has no variables.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed pp.133--134, simultaneous-root algebra and essential surjectivity; algebraic expansion of the Abhyankar input.

proof.text:
Put $V_i=R_{\mathfrak p_i}$ and $A_i=B_{\mathfrak q_i}$. The principal-prime localization criterion says that both are DVRs, with uniformizers $t_i$ and $x_i$. In fact $B\otimes_R V_i=A_i$: after quotient by $x_i$, this finite $V_i$-algebra is the generic fibre of the domain $B/(x_i)$ over $R/(t_i)$, hence is a field. Every maximal ideal over the maximal ideal of $V_i$ contains $x_i$, since $t_i=x_i^n$. Thus there is exactly one maximal ideal, and the displayed finite algebra is already local, with localization $A_i$. It follows that $V_i\to A_i$ is finite and faithful, with fraction fields $K\to E$, and
$$\mathfrak m_{V_i}A_i=(t_i)=(x_i^n)=\mathfrak m_{A_i}^{n}.$$
In particular both primes have height one. Any height-one prime of $B$ containing $f=\prod_i x_i^n$ contains some $x_i$ and therefore equals $\mathfrak q_i$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed pp.133--134, simultaneous-root algebra and essential surjectivity; algebraic expansion of the Abhyankar input.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $j$. The Galois degree bound for normalization over a DVR applies to $L_j/K$ over $V_i$, because $[L_j:K]\mid n$. At every prime of the integral closure of $V_i$ in $L_j$ above $\mathfrak m_{V_i}$, both ramification index and residue degree divide $n$. This closure is finite by the separable integral-closure theorem. The integer $n$ is a unit in $V_i$, so these are exactly the invertibility and divisibility hypotheses required by the DVR tame tensor-factor lemma.

For a factor $F_a$ of $L_j\otimes_K E$, it is also a maximal field quotient of $L_j\otimes_{V_i} A_i$: in this tensor product $t_i$ is invertible through $L_j$, so it equals $L_j\otimes_K E$. The map $A_i\to F_a$ is injective. Its integral closure $S_a$ is finite because $A_i$ is a Noetherian normal DVR and $F_a/E$ is finite separable. Apply the DVR tame tensor-factor unramifiedness theorem with base DVR $V_i$, root DVR $A_i$, and exponent $n$. By Step 6 the root index is exactly $n$; Step 7 supplies both divisibilities. It yields $\Omega_{(S_a)_Q/A_i}=0$ for every prime $Q$ above $\mathfrak m_{A_i}$. Integral-closure localization identifies $S_a=C_a\otimes_B A_i$. Hence for every prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $C_a$ above $\mathfrak q_i$ one has $\Omega_{(C_a)_{\mathfrak Q}/B_{\mathfrak q_i}}=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BRM (lemma-abhyankar), through the cited DVR tensor-factor theorem; Tag 0307 for localization.

proof.text: For a height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ outside $V(f)$, Step 4 identifies the normalization with the finite etale cover $P_B$, so it is etale there. Each $C_a$ is finitely presented over $B$ because it is finite over the Noetherian base. The pointwise etale criterion therefore gives zero relative differentials at each such prime. Every remaining height-one prime is some $\mathfrak q_i$ by Step 6, and Step 8 gives the vanishing of the corresponding relative differential modules. Apply finite-normalization codimension-one purity separately to $B\subset C_a\subset F_a$. Its hypotheses are regular Noetherian domain $B$, finite separable $F_a/E$, finite $C_a$, and precisely these vanishing statements. Each $\operatorname{Spec}C_a\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale. The finite-product etale theorem then makes $N=\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ finite etale.

source.place: Tag 0BMB (pione-lemma-purity), applied to the finite normalization; finite products of etale algebras.

proof.text: The map $N\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is surjective. Indeed its finite image is closed, and contains the generic point because $P_B$ is a nonempty torsor over the nonempty $U_B$; the generic algebra $D$ is nonzero. Since $B$ is a domain, a closed set containing its generic point is all of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Apply the etale-section theorem for finite algebras over a strictly henselian ring with $H=A=B$. It gives a section $s:\operatorname{Spec}B\to N$. Restricting $s$ to $U_B$ and composing with the isomorphism of Step 4 gives a section $s_U:U_B\to P_B$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, printed pp.133--134, simultaneous-root algebra and essential surjectivity; algebraic expansion of the Abhyankar input.

proof.text: Pull the torsor identity $G\times P_B\cong P_B\times_{U_B}P_B$, $(g,p)\mapsto(gp,p)$, back along $s_U$ in the second factor. Its source becomes $G\times U_B=\coprod_{g\in G}U_B$ and its target becomes $P_B$. Thus the resulting isomorphism has on the $g$-th summand the explicit map $u\mapsto g\,s_U(u)$ and commutes with the structure maps to $U_B$. Inverting it is the requested isomorphism. This is an application of the defining torsor identity, with no connectedness hypothesis on the total space. If $r=0$, all boundary-prime steps are empty, $B=R$ and $f=1$, and the same section argument applies directly to $P$; if $n=1$, the roots and the one-element torsor give the identity case.
